junro.title: Prioritree UX — the web-app tier worked through prior to the MCP surface: the human comparator's vote surface over the core's five-op interface — FastAPI-served, the entire front end projected from Python (Shoelace chrome, HTMX wire, Jinja2 render, Web Components under separation of concerns), CQRS-shaped backend communication, lifecycle make targets — the full junro, all seats participating
inputs: the collaborator's rulings of 2026-11-22 (the UX ask prior to the MCP surface; the stack re-anchor: Shoelace + HTMX + separation-of-concerns Web Components, all frontend things generated from Python — the front end a projection from Python things; the CQRS agenda; the existing FastAPI server; lifecycle make targets; the full-junro all-seats mandate)

Q-frontend-stack's ruling at the prioritree-birth store (2026-11-19): HTMX carries UX-to-backend, Shoelace via CDN, Web Components under separation of concerns, Jinja2 always, generated from structure, hand-authored frontend out of grammar

Q-setup-arch's ruled four-form architecture (prioritree-birth): library-first, the CLI wraps, FastAPI serves, the web fronts — the web-app tier is the human comparator's vote surface, opening on the core library's public-face gate (green: prioritree-core done)
the core's five-op interface (Q-solution-space, prioritree-core): register_run, next_pair, cast_vote, read_vote_state, tally_rank — the surface this effort fronts
Q-mcp-surface's banked ruling (prioritree-core): the MCP surface composes when the service era arrives — this effort is prior to it

structure.purpose: THE PER-UNIT PIPELINE (the core store's precedent): THE CENSUS FIRST — ungated tansa/shindan/rikai packets over the existing ground (the FastAPI server, the tech notes, the current web state; shindan naming the API's current error shape — R5's census clause); then THE DESIGN LANE — ungated suisen/keisan/hyoka/moho packets; then togo's gated synthesis closing G-UX-DESIGN-BRIEF; each build unit's ungated discovery legs + gated brief precede its build; THE ROUTE GROWS UNIT-BY-UNIT (each build unit's pair auto-stamps at its build-add; its rich build gate mints before — the composition model).
structure.entry_condition: G-COMPOSITION is green (the composition validated at the route's head); the census fires first, its findings assumed by none of this composition.

structure.purpose: THE WEB TIER'S BUILD — the ruled unit set, one module per dispatch (the sizing law): service (the existing FastAPI server grown into the CQRS lanes over the core's five ops — R2; every touched API surface brought into ThreePart compliance as-we-go — R5, no separate remediation unit), web (the entire front end projected from Python — Shoelace via CDN, Web Components under separation of concerns, HTMX, Jinja2 always, generated from structure; hand-authored artifacts out of grammar — R1; the web fronts the service — Q-setup-arch's layering), lifecycle (the Makefile's service-management targets, start/stop/etc. — R3: "room for service targets later" is now); each lands per its approved brief (the exact-task law), kensho's independent verification per build gate, one-commit-per-increment.
structure.entry_condition: G-UX-DESIGN-BRIEF is green — the design is the spec; each unit's own G-<UNIT>-BRIEF green before its dispatch (the precedence law).

structure.purpose: THE EFFORT'S BOOKEND (the birth store's close form): hansei's retro (R4's debrief seat — the friction ledger the intake), the effort's records (the MCP-surface era named next, Q-mcp-surface banked — this effort prior to it), the done call at the collaborator's ruling.
structure.entry_condition: the route's build gates closed green and the collaborator has called the close.

conditions: the composition lands at the store's evidence home (.junro/evidence/Q-ux-surface/route-composition*.md — the set: the stages spine, gates-a, gates-b, increments) — the opening whole: stages, gates, increments, the census placed FIRST with none of its findings assumed, every seat placed (R4: no seat bypassed)

every choice cites its ruling: R1–R5 + the birth store's precedents (Q-frontend-stack's projection law, Q-solution-space's five-op interface, Q-setup-arch's web-app tier) + the core store's pipeline precedent

the collaborator validates the composition — the gate is the validation (the birth store's composition-validation entry condition, carried as the route's head gate); the outcome records against compose/route; no route dispatch fires before it is green

THE DESIGN BRIEF LANDED: togo's synthesis over the census (census/ground, census/error-shape, census/mechanism) + the design lane (design/flows, design/cqrs-mapping, design/presentation, design/adversarial, design/blind-walk); a divergence that survives reconciliation blocks the brief, never rides it silently (the pipeline-parallelism safeguard)

the brief carries the design-work whole R1/R2 leave open — never settled in the composition: the UX flows (the comparator's journey over the five ops), the CQRS op-mapping (the ops' command/query lanes at the service surface + the HTMX wire's lanes — cited back to R2), the tally presentation (the ranked whole rendered from tally_rank's frozen result — tie groups, coverage data, the safe halt shown honestly), the projection architecture (the front end's source structure + its Python generator — R1)

the brief carries the ThreePart remediation map (R5): the census's error-shape diagnosis folded forward — every build unit's brief names the API surfaces it touches + their expected/found/next-action compliance plan
THE COLLABORATOR'S APPROVAL: the design judged ready-to-build; the build units' briefs cite it; their dispatches fire only after their own brief gates green
hansei's retro landed: the debrief over the effort whole, the friction ledger the intake, the lessons named
the effort's records landed: the CONTINUATION entry (the landing state named honestly); the MCP-surface era named next (banked, not composed)
the collaborator rules the close — the done call recorded same-turn; the route's status set done at the ruling (the birth store's G-BIRTH-RECORDS form)

amendments.what: add-ruling {"question": "Q-ux-surface", "ruling": "THE ERROR SHAPE, MANDATORY (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, verbatim ground: \"the api absolutely does not follow the errors teach methodology. So, we are going to have to fix that as we go. The ThreePart is mandatory in this codebase now.\"): the existing FastAPI API does not follow the errors-teach methodology — and the fix rides this effort as-we-go (no separate remediation effort; each unit that touches an API surface brings that surface into compliance as it lands). THE THREEPART IS MANDATORY IN THIS CODEBASE NOW: every error response carries expected / found / next-action — the shape this codebase's own instruments already teach (the junro engine's every refusal: \"REFUSED — Expected: ... Found: ... Next-action: ...\"; the core's ruled refusals — Q-granularity R2's \"expected/found/next-action naming the legal set\", R12's SAFE HALT \"carrying expected/found/next-action naming the isolated items/components and the exact closing pairs\"). At the API: every 4xx/5xx response body is a ThreePart error — expected (the legal state named), found (what the request actually carried / what occurred), next-action (the named cure or legal form — self-correcting) — never a bare status code, never a stack leak, never a silent OK where a refusal belongs. Every build unit of this route inherits this: the units touching the API bring the touched surfaces into ThreePart compliance as-we-go."}

amendments.what: add-ruling {"question": "Q-ux-surface", "ruling": "THE REPORT AUTHORSHIP LAW (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, verbatim ground: \"the seats write their reports via the report op... translating from returns is not how we do things anymore... each seat is supposed to write its own report.\"): every dispatched seat writes its own completion report via the junro packet report op — actor = the seat, packet = its packet, content = the seat's own report in its own words; the report rides the ledger from the seat's own actor stamp. shinko NEVER translates a seat's return into a report — the convenor's ledger duties are the machinery events alone (dispatch, result, gate) and the evidence landing (the result's output artifact); the report is the member's act, the member's voice. THE STANDING DISPATCH FORM: every dispatch prompt carries the report step — \"file your completion report via the junro packet report op (actor=<seat>, packet=<id>, store=<path>) before returning\" — a dispatch without the report step is out of grammar. THE TRANSITION (this effort): the three census packets' shinko-recorded reports (census/ground, census/error-shape, census/mechanism) were filed pre-correction in the translation form — they stand as the machinery's pre-correction records, SUPERSEDED by the seats' own reports when the seats file them (append-only; the seat-authored reports are the packet's authoritative voice); the design packets' reports (design/flows, design/cqrs-mapping, design/presentation) are filed by their seats from the start — no translated report ever lands for them."}

open_questions.question: What is the UX for Priori-tree's human comparator — the web-app tier's vote surface over the core's five-op interface (register_run, next_pair, cast_vote, read_vote_state, tally_rank), FastAPI-served, the entire front end projected from Python (Shoelace chrome, HTMX wire, Jinja2 render, Web Components under separation of concerns), CQRS-shaped backend communication, lifecycle make targets — worked through prior to the MCP surface?

rulings.text: THE UX STACK, RE-ANCHORED (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, restating Q-frontend-stack at the prioritree-birth store for this effort): Shoelace for the CSS and web components (via CDN); separation-of-concerns architecture (Web Components); HTMX for backend communication; Jinja2 templating always; generated from structure — and the entire front end is a projection from Python things: ALL frontend things are generated from Python, including the entire Web Components surface. Hand-authored frontend artifacts are out of grammar; the web surface regenerates from its source structure (the content-in-configuration law at the web tier; the never-hand-edit-cycle-generated-files law inherited there).

THE CQRS AGENDA (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, verbatim: "We run a CQRS agenda. Command Query Response Segregation."): the web tier's backend communication segregates commands (the state-changing acts) from queries (the state reads) at the service surface, served by the existing FastAPI server over the core's five-op interface. The concrete op-mapping and the HTMX wire's command/query lanes compose in this effort's design work, cited back to this ruling.

THE SERVICE GROUND AND LIFECYCLE TARGETS (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22): an existing FastAPI server is in place — the setup skeleton's ruled API tier (Q-setup-arch at prioritree-birth: "the FastAPI service serves it") — and the effort grows the Makefile's lifecycle management targets (start, stop, etc.): "room for service targets later" (the birth ruling's own clause) is now.

THE GOVERNANCE FORM (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22): this effort is managed via a full junro — all team member participation: every seat rides the route — keikaku composes; tansa, shindan, and rikai discover and diagnose; suisen and keisan recommend and calculate; hyoka assesses adversarially; moho blind-walks; togo synthesizes and integrates; jikko executes; kensho verifies; hansei debriefs; shinko dispatches. No seat is bypassed; the route's composition realizes this mandate.

THE ERROR SHAPE, MANDATORY (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, verbatim ground: "the api absolutely does not follow the errors teach methodology. So, we are going to have to fix that as we go. The ThreePart is mandatory in this codebase now."): the existing FastAPI API does not follow the errors-teach methodology — and the fix rides this effort as-we-go (no separate remediation effort; each unit that touches an API surface brings that surface into compliance as it lands). THE THREEPART IS MANDATORY IN THIS CODEBASE NOW: every error response carries expected / found / next-action — the shape this codebase's own instruments already teach (the junro engine's every refusal: "REFUSED — Expected: ... Found: ... Next-action: ..."; the core's ruled refusals — Q-granularity R2's "expected/found/next-action naming the legal set", R12's SAFE HALT "carrying expected/found/next-action naming the isolated items/components and the exact closing pairs"). At the API: every 4xx/5xx response body is a ThreePart error — expected (the legal state named), found (what the request actually carried / what occurred), next-action (the named cure or legal form — self-correcting) — never a bare status code, never a stack leak, never a silent OK where a refusal belongs. Every build unit of this route inherits this: the units touching the API bring the touched surfaces into ThreePart compliance as-we-go.

THE REPORT AUTHORSHIP LAW (collaborator ruling, 2026-11-22, verbatim ground: "the seats write their reports via the report op... translating from returns is not how we do things anymore... each seat is supposed to write its own report."): every dispatched seat writes its own completion report via the junro packet report op — actor = the seat, packet = its packet, content = the seat's own report in its own words; the report rides the ledger from the seat's own actor stamp. shinko NEVER translates a seat's return into a report — the convenor's ledger duties are the machinery events alone (dispatch, result, gate) and the evidence landing (the result's output artifact); the report is the member's act, the member's voice. THE STANDING DISPATCH FORM: every dispatch prompt carries the report step — "file your completion report via the junro packet report op (actor=<seat>, packet=<id>, store=<path>) before returning" — a dispatch without the report step is out of grammar. THE TRANSITION (this effort): the three census packets' shinko-recorded reports (census/ground, census/error-shape, census/mechanism) were filed pre-correction in the translation form — they stand as the machinery's pre-correction records, SUPERSEDED by the seats' own reports when the seats file them (append-only; the seat-authored reports are the packet's authoritative voice); the design packets' reports (design/flows, design/cqrs-mapping, design/presentation) are filed by their seats from the start — no translated report ever lands for them.
